madhurā.notes: MN 84 places King Avantiputta and Mahākaccāna at Madhurā. MN 83 takes place at Mithilā. The road to Verañjā is in AN 4.53, and the five drawbacks of Madhurā are in AN 5.220.

magadha.notes: The comparison with Magadhan village fields is in AN 5.100. The adjacent AN 5.99 describes a lion.

magha.notes: SN 11.12:1.3 and SN 11.13:6.1 explicitly name the student Magha as Sakka in his human life. SN 11.11 gives the seven vows. The page matches at SN 11.9, SN 11.10, and SN 11.14 do not supply the name or the vows.

mahisavatthu.notes: AN 8.8:1.1 places Uttara on Saṅkheyyaka Mountain in the Mahisa region. The local Pali reads vaṭajālikāyaṁ where the entry gives Dhavajālika.

mahākaccāna.notes: AN 1.197 names the foremost exponent of brief statements, and MN 18 shows him explaining one. The cited verses occur at Thag 8.1, whose attribution spells his name Mahākaccāyano. Several page matches miss their episode. The Madhurā visit is in MN 84, the meeting with Kāḷī in AN 10.26, and the Lohicca encounter in SN 35.132. AN 5.165–166 both open with Sāriputta.

mahāli.notes: Mahāli the Licchavi asks about Sakka in SN 11.13 and Pūraṇa Kassapa in SN 22.60. SN 11.12 and SN 22.59 are neighboring discourses. AN 10.50:15.3 is a chapter recap.

mahānāma.notes: AN 1.252 names the Sakyan foremost in giving fine things. AN 5.58:3.1 explicitly calls the walker in the Great Wood a Licchavi. MN 116 names a paccekabuddha, and Thag 1.115 and the recap in Thag 1.120 name an elder. Neither has a candidate entry here. AN 8.30, AN 11.21, SN 55.30, and SN 55.40 mention Mahānāma only in chapter recaps. In Snp 5.19:25.4 mahānāmo describes the third chapter. The Sakyan’s lodging search is in AN 3.126 and his question about concentration and knowledge in AN 3.73. SN 54.12 is his conversation with Lomasakaṅgiya, and SN 11.3 is about Sakka’s banner.

mahāpāragā.notes: The Great Congregation names this group immediately after the Pāragas at DN 20:16.7. The printed DN.ii.26 citation lands in DN 14.

mahāsammata.notes: The citation is unplaced in the packet. DN 27:20.3–21.1 recounts the election, the share of rice, and the origin of the title Mahāsammata.

mahāvana.notes: AN 9.41:1.1–1.6 locates the Buddha’s daytime retreat at Uruvelakappa in the land of the Mallas, and Tapussa and Ānanda visit him there. The packet cites AN 9.40. Its zero mention count also misses the Vesālī forest in AN 8.53:1.1 and the Kapilavatthu forest in SN 1.37:1.2. Sujato calls all three the Great Wood. The two DPD forests need their own dictionary coverage.

mahī.notes: The five-river list includes Mahī in the Pali of SN 13.3:1.3, SN 13.4:1.3, SN 55.42:5.2, SN 56.53:1.2, and SN 56.54:1.2. Each is missing from the packet because the English names the rivers one segment earlier. The page match SN 13.5 concerns the earth.

makkhaligosāla.notes: Snp 3.6:2.2 writes the teacher’s name as one word. DN 2:19.1 writes makkhali gosālo separately and recounts his teaching. AN 3.137 and AN 6.57 are the relevant discourses in their cited clusters. SN 22.60 quotes Pūraṇa Kassapa, as the entry observes.

mallikā.notes: SN 3.8 and Ud 5.1 name Pasenadi and his queen together. The report of their daughter’s birth is in SN 3.16, the news of Mallikā’s death in AN 5.49, and the meeting hall in her park in DN 9 and MN 78. AN 8.91–117 lists a laywoman called Mallikā without a royal title.

mandākinī.notes: AN 7.66:6.2–6.3 lists Mandākinī among the great lakes from which the rivers flow. The entry covers the lake portion of the combined DPD gloss.

manopadosikā.notes: The packet misses all mentions. DN 1:2.10.2 and DN 24:2.19.9 explicitly say manopadosikā nāma devā and describe their mutual anger. DN 20:16.4 names the group at the Great Congregation. Sujato translates the name as ‘malevolent’.

mantāṇī.notes: MN 86:12.11–12.12 identifies Aṅgulimāla’s mother. The king asks for his parents’ clans, and Sujato renders the answer ‘my mother a Mantāṇī’. The DPD example MN 24 gives Puṇṇa’s matronymic Mantāṇiputta and supplies no link between the two mothers.

maṅgala.notes: MN 116:5.2–5.3 introduces the names of those who awakened independently. Maṅgala appears in that list at 6.29.

maṇibhadda.notes: The exchange about freedom from enmity is in SN 10.4. The local Pali calls the shrine Maṇimālika where the entry has Maṇimālaka. SN 10.3 and SN 10.5 are neighboring discourses, and SN 10.12:14.2 is a chapter recap.
